## Black Stone Minerals, L.P. Reports Third Quarter Results


11/02/2026


[Download (opens in new window) PDF 230 KB](https://s202.q4cdn.com/437079403/files/doc_financials/2026/q3/Black-Stone-Minerals-L-P-Reports-Third-Quarter-Results-2026.pdf)


HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Black Stone Minerals, L.P. (NYSE: BSM) ("Black Stone Minerals," "Black Stone," or "the Partnership") today announces its financial and operating results for the third quarter of 2026.


**Financial and Operational Highlights**


- Net income for the third quarter was $52.4 million, and Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter totaled $104.1 million.
- Distributable cash flow was $93.0 million for the third quarter.
- Mineral and royalty production for the third quarter of 2026 equaled 34.5 MBoe/d, an increase of 6% from the prior quarter; total production, including working-interest volumes, was 35.6 MBoe/d for the quarter.
- Black Stone announced a distribution attributable to the third quarter of 2026 of $0.35 per common unit, or $1.40 annualized, up 9% from the prior quarter and 17% since the first quarter. Distribution coverage was 1.25x.
- Total debt at the end of the third quarter was $195.0 million; as of October 30, 2026, total debt was $197.0 million with $5.4 million of cash on hand.


**Management Commentary**


Taylor DeWalch, Co-CEO and President, commented, “We are pleased with another strong quarter, reflecting increased development activity and higher oil production and revenue. Continued leasing efforts and active portfolio management have helped promote further development of our oil acreage, providing additional cash flow in the current commodity price environment as our natural gas development programs continue to ramp. This performance supported our second consecutive quarterly distribution increase while allowing Black Stone to maintain prudent distribution coverage, financial flexibility, and a strong balance sheet.


“We also continue to execute on opportunities to enhance the long-term value of our asset base, highlighted by a successful marketing process and the significant expansion of our Caturus development agreement in the Shelby Trough. Together, these results reflect the strength of our current portfolio and continued execution of our long-term growth strategy as we work to drive development and increase returns for our unitholders.”


Fowler Carter, Co-CEO and President, added, “The addition of two significant development areas and an associated long-term development program meaningfully expands our Caturus program and the development footprint within Black Stone’s expanded Shelby Trough position. Continued execution under our Adamas development agreement, progress on initial development under our Revenant agreement, and increasing activity from other operators across our broader Shelby Trough acreage further demonstrate the growing development opportunity across our position. We believe the scale of this inventory, combined with our ability to work with operators and capital providers to establish long-term development programs, positions Black Stone well as the industry prepares to meet anticipated growth in natural gas demand.


“LNG exports, power generation, and other sources of demand will require significant long-term natural gas supply, and we believe Black Stone is well positioned to help provide the drilling inventory needed to support that growth. Our strategy has been to assemble large, high-interest mineral positions in the expanded Shelby Trough, contiguous to our legacy assets, and place that acreage into structured development programs. The expanded Caturus agreement increases the acreage and long-term drilling inventory subject to structured development programs, further advancing development of Black Stone’s Shelby Trough position.”


**Quarterly Financial and Operating Results**


*Production*


Black Stone reported mineral and royalty volumes of 34.5 MBoe/d (73% natural gas) for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 32.5 MBoe/d for the second quarter of 2026 and 34.7 MBoe/d for the third quarter of 2025.


Working-interest production was 1.1 MBoe/d for the third quarter of 2026, 1.0 MBoe/d in the second quarter of 2026, and 1.6 MBoe/d for the third quarter of 2025.


Total reported production averaged 35.6 MBoe/d (97% mineral and royalty, 73% natural gas) for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 33.5 MBoe/d and 36.3 MBoe/d for the second quarter of 2026 and the third quarter of 2025, respectively.


*Realized Prices, Revenues, and Net Income*


The Partnership’s average realized price per Boe, excluding the effect of derivative settlements, was $37.44 for the third quarter of 2026. This is a decrease of 1% from $37.82 per Boe in the second quarter of 2026 and a 25% increase from $30.01 in the third quarter of 2025.


Black Stone reported oil and gas revenue of $122.7 million (63% oil and condensate) for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 6% from $115.4 million in the second quarter of 2026. Oil and gas revenue in the third quarter of 2025 was $100.2 million.


The Partnership reported a loss on commodity derivative instruments of $30.2 million for the third quarter of 2026, composed of a $0.4 million loss from realized settlements and a non-cash $29.8 million unrealized loss due to the change in value of Black Stone’s derivative positions during the quarter. Black Stone reported a gain of $26.8 million and a gain of $27.3 million on commodity derivative instruments for the second quarter of 2026 and the third quarter of 2025, respectively.


Lease bonus and other income was $7.2 million for the third quarter of 2026. Lease bonus and other income for the second quarter of 2026 and the third quarter of 2025 was $6.7 million and $5.0 million, respectively.


The Partnership reported net income of $52.4 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to net income of $106.4 million in the preceding quarter. For the third quarter of 2025, the Partnership reported net income of $91.7 million.


*Adjusted EBITDA and Distributable Cash Flow*


Adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026 was $104.1 million, which compares to $91.3 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $88.1 million in the third quarter of 2025. Distributable cash flow for the third quarter of 2026 was $93.0 million. For the second quarter of 2026 and the third quarter of 2025, distributable cash flow was $80.4 million and $78.6 million, respectively.


*Financial* **** *Position and Activities*


As of September 30, 2026, Black Stone had $5.5 million in cash, with $195.0 million drawn under its credit facility. As of October 30, 2026, the Partnership had $5.4 million in cash, with $197.0 million outstanding under the credit facility. Black Stone is in compliance with all financial covenants associated with its credit facility.


On October 30, 2026, the borrowing base under the credit facility was reaffirmed at $580.0 million and the Partnership elected to maintain total commitments under the credit facility at $375.0 million. The Partnership's next regularly scheduled borrowing base redetermination is set for April 2027.


*Third Quarter 2026 Distributions*


As previously announced, the Board approved a cash distribution of $0.35 for each common unit attributable to the third quarter of 2026, representing a 9% increase over the prior quarter and a 17% increase from the $0.30 per unit distribution attributable to the first quarter of 2026. Distribution coverage for the quarter was approximately 1.25x. The distribution will be payable on November 13, 2026, to unitholders of record as of the close of business on November 6, 2026.


**Activity Update**


*Development Activity*


As of the end of the third quarter, Adamas Energy ("Adamas") was operating two rigs on Black Stone’s Angelina and San Augustine acreage in the Shelby Trough. During the third quarter, Adamas successfully turned to sales 7 gross (0.7 net) wells. Adamas’s development program remains on track with the development agreements, with a total of 14 wells spud in the previous program year that ended on June 30, 2026. Of these wells, 9 gross (0.9 net) have turned to sales as of September 30, 2026, and 4 gross (0.4 net) are expected to turn to sales during the fourth quarter of 2026, with the remaining well under further evaluation. As of September 30, 2026, Adamas spud 6 of the total 17 wells expected to be drilled in the current program year ending on June 30, 2027.


Black Stone’s agreement with Revenant Energy ("Revenant") covers 270,000 gross acres in which Black Stone currently controls approximately 122,000 undeveloped net acres, primarily located in Angelina, Nacogdoches, and San Augustine counties in Texas. The agreement includes minimum annual drilling commitments across three designated areas of interest ("AOIs"), measured by wells drilled in 2026 and completed gross lateral feet beginning in 2027. In September 2026, the Partnership entered into an amendment to the agreement that increased the overall 2027 drilling commitment by 7,000 gross lateral feet while extending until 2029 the requirement that a portion of the drilling commitment be completed in a second AOI. For 2026, Revenant is expected to meet its 4-well drilling commitment. As of the end of the third quarter, Revenant was operating one rig and had drilled 2 wells expected to turn to sales by year-end. Revenant spud the remaining 2 wells in early October 2026, with production expected in mid-2027.


In November 2025, the Partnership entered into a 220,000 gross acre development agreement with an affiliate of Caturus Energy, LLC ("Caturus") covering acreage primarily in Angelina, Cherokee, Houston, and Nacogdoches counties in Texas, which aims to push the Shelby Trough westward toward the Western Haynesville. Development activity under the original agreement is underway. Caturus drilled a pilot well in Cherokee County in the third quarter of 2026 and, in October 2026, spud its first 2 development wells, which are expected to begin production in the first half of 2027.


In October 2026, the Partnership entered into an amended and restated development agreement with Caturus that expands the contract area by 730,000 gross acres to a total of 950,000 gross acres and provides for incremental development commitments across two additional development areas primarily located in Houston, Trinity, and Polk counties in Texas. Consistent with the original agreement, minimum annual drilling commitments are measured in completed lateral feet net to Black Stone’s mineral ownership. The level of gross well activity associated with these commitments depends on well locations, lateral lengths, and Black Stone’s mineral ownership in the acreage developed. Each additional development area includes an initial pilot phase and a multi-year development program designed to ramp activity over time. Development activity in the first additional area is expected to begin with a pilot well by the first quarter of 2028 and, if Caturus elects to proceed following the pilot phase, would be followed by 2 gross wells in 2029 and a ramp to approximately 12 gross wells annually by 2034, as minimum annual drilling commitments increase from 8,000 to 33,600 net lateral feet over the same period. Caturus has the option to initiate development activity in the second additional area and, if elected, would begin with a pilot well by the end of 2031 and, if Caturus elects to proceed following the pilot phase, would be followed by 2 gross wells in 2033 and a ramp to approximately 12 gross wells annually by 2038, as minimum annual drilling commitments increase from 8,000 to 33,600 net lateral feet over the same period. The amended and restated agreement also provides Caturus flexibility to satisfy a portion of its annual development commitments for each development area through drilling in the other development areas, subject to certain minimum annual development requirements within each area.


In the Permian Basin, Blue Arrow Operating is progressing a 25 gross (1.9 net) well development on Black Stone’s acreage in the southern Delaware Basin. As of September 30, 2026, 10 gross (0.9 net) wells had been turned to sales, with the remaining wells expected to come online in the fourth quarter of 2026 and first half of 2027.


*Acquisition Activity*


The Partnership continues to acquire bolt-on acreage in multiple contractual development programs with significant inventory at high net interests across San Augustine, Nacogdoches, Angelina, Cherokee, Houston, and Trinity counties.


In the third quarter of 2026, consistent with the previously announced acquisition strategy, Black Stone acquired $14.6 million of additional (primarily non-producing) mineral and royalty interests. In October 2026, Black Stone acquired additional mineral and royalty interests and surface rights in the expanded Shelby Trough area from various sellers for $30.6 million in cash and $2.1 million in common units of the Partnership. The Partnership acquired the surface rights on a strategic tract to secure additional drilling locations in support of Black Stone's development agreements, and the acquisition included additional consideration tied to future production.


From September 2023 through October 2026, the Partnership completed $335.5 million of acquisitions, primarily consisting of mineral and royalty interests in the expanded Shelby Trough area. Black Stone’s commercial strategy going forward includes the continuation of meaningful, targeted mineral and royalty acquisitions to complement the Partnership's existing positions.

**About Black Stone Minerals, L.P.**


Black Stone Minerals is one of the largest owners and managers of oil and natural gas mineral interests in the United States. The Partnership owns mineral interests and royalty interests in 41 states in the continental United States. Black Stone believes its large, diversified asset base and long-lived, non-cost-bearing mineral and royalty interests provide for stable production and reserves over time, allowing the majority of generated cash flow to be distributed to unitholders.

**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


Adjusted EBITDA and Distributable Cash Flow are supplemental non-GAAP financial measures used by Black Stone’s management and external users of the Partnership’s financial statements such as investors, research analysts, and others, to assess the financial performance of its assets and its ability to sustain distributions over the long term without regard to financing methods, capital structure, or historical cost basis.


The Partnership defines Adjusted EBITDA as net income (loss) before interest expense, income taxes, and depreciation, depletion, and amortization adjusted for impairment of oil and natural gas properties, if any, accretion of asset retirement obligations, seismic data acquisition costs, non-cash equity-based compensation, unrealized gains and losses on commodity derivative instruments, and gains and losses on sales of assets, if any. Black Stone defines Distributable Cash Flow as Adjusted EBITDA plus or minus amounts for certain non-cash operating activities, cash interest expense, distributions to preferred unitholders, and restructuring charges, if any.


Beginning with the three months and year ended December 31, 2025, the Partnership revised its definition of Adjusted EBITDA to exclude seismic data acquisition costs, which are included in Exploration expense on the Partnership’s consolidated statements of operations. Comparative amounts for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, for each of Adjusted EBITDA and Distributable Cash Flow have been recast to conform to the current period presentation. Management believes this revised definition enhances comparability between periods and reflects the Partnership’s view of seismic data acquisition costs as investments that support the long-term development and value of its mineral and royalty interests.


Adjusted EBITDA and Distributable Cash Flow should not be considered an alternative to, or more meaningful than, net income (loss), income (loss) from operations, cash flows from operating activities, or any other measure of financial performance presented in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles ("GAAP") in the United States as measures of the Partnership’s financial performance.


Adjusted EBITDA and Distributable Cash Flow have important limitations as analytical tools because they exclude some but not all items that affect net income (loss), the most directly comparable U.S. GAAP financial measure. The Partnership’s computation of Adjusted EBITDA and Distributable Cash Flow may differ from computations of similarly titled measures of other companies.
